M2 forecast training

Source: vignettes/articles/forecast-training.qmd

Caution

This is a source-level training example, not verified production evidence. Private historical metrics and promoted artifacts are not distributed with the package. Complete acceptance, fixed-spec refresh, and immutable promotion before calling any fit a deployment.

M2 forecasts positivity one and two weeks ahead with a binomial GAM. Its covariates include current surveillance features and M1 outputs constructed at the same issue week.

Fit and specify 

library(PAGe)

m2_grid <- if (exists("prior_m2_results", inherits = FALSE)) {
  plan_m2_grid(prior_m2_results, max_finalists = 6L, max_specs = 64L)
} else {
  default_m2_grid()
}
m2_tuning <- tune_m2(
  historical, selection, m0, m1,
  grid = m2_grid
)
validate_m2_tuning(m2_tuning)
draft_m2 <- fit_m2(
  historical, selection, m0, m1,
  config = m2_tuning$best_spec
)
m2 <- freeze_m2(draft_m2, tuning = m2_tuning)

After validate_m2_tuning() passes, m2 is the frozen M2 candidate stage. The full candidate is assembled only after frozen M0 and M1 are available:

candidate <- assemble_kit(m0, m1, m2)
validate_page_kit(candidate)
saveRDS(candidate, "results/candidate_pre_holdout.rds")

The default grid contains the current v16-corrected incumbent values (delta=0, Kr=1, k_f=4, k_e=2, alpha_state=0.20, k_r=0, k_de=0, k_sp=8, bias_alpha=0.05, and bias_beta=0), but their presence is not proof of a deployed kit. Use walk-forward LOSO before proposing a different specification, then complete the governed holdout and promotion sequence.

Both m0 and m1 above must already be frozen governed artifacts with the same selection; M2 verifies their upstream identity link before tuning or fitting. train_m2() remains the legacy-compatible fitting implementation.

Grid expansion

M2 grids grow quickly. Prefer plan_m2_grid(previous_results, max_finalists, max_specs): it retains the coded incumbent and diverse finalists, adds nearest local neighbors, and proposes one valid adjacent step beyond winning boundaries.

Treat basis sizes as integer complexity controls and expand one step at a time. Zero for optional terms such as k_r or k_de is a meaningful feature-off null, not a reason to propose negative values. Expand alpha_state locally inside its valid decay domain. Keep an unidentifiable runtime correction fixed rather than adding it to the search merely because it is configurable.

Apply the declared minimum-NLL, one-standard-error, or Pareto rule only after all surviving candidates have complete comparable LOSO folds. A grid cap with a remaining boundary is an unresolved search, not proof of an optimum.

Historical M2 training uses leave-one-season-out folds with fold-specific reference and M1 feature construction. M0 and M1 hyperparameters were selected before the M2 folds, so this is conditional M2 validation rather than fully nested selection of the entire pipeline.

For each fold, the held-out season must also be absent from manual_labels_train, with manual_labels_test = NULL, so its ignition timing is detected prospectively. A checkpoint evaluated with the held-out manual label is leaked and must be recomputed.

Frozen model and online correction

The frozen runtime uses a level-only correction with base bias_alpha=0.05, bias_beta=0, and high bias_alpha=0.7 after two same-sign transitions (the third consecutive same-sign residual). The season-specific effect is estimated online from eligible post-ignition observations. Both updates must use errors whose targets are already observed at the issue date.

Use Bernoulli negative log likelihood as the primary probabilistic score and retain horizon-specific calibration and absolute-error summaries. Pooling only across all weeks can conceal poor performance near ignition or the seasonal peak.
